idiom_name: Rails view helper modules (app/helpers) over ActionView::Helpers
implementation_notes: Rails bakes the pattern in: ActionView::Helpers supplies the built-in presentation helpers (number_to_currency, time_ago_in_words, truncate, pluralize), and a custom helper is a module in app/helpers that Rails mixes into every view automatically - a method is the whole structure, with no helper class and no registration call. Helpers execute in the view context, so they can call other helpers and the tag builder, and the framework's escaping applies to whatever they return unless the helper opts out with html_safe. Keep ActiveRecord queries in the controller or model: a helper that queries is the classic Rails view wart. A helper class is justified only when the logic must carry shared configuration or memoized state; Rails' module model needs none of that for a plain formatting rule.
code_sketch:
# app/helpers/pricing_helper.rb   (auto-included in every view)
module PricingHelper
  def money(cents, currency = "EUR")
    tag.span(number_to_currency(cents / 100.0, unit: currency), class: "money")
  end
end

# view:  <%= money(order.total) %>        <%# no require, no registration %>
pitfalls: Every helper module is mixed into every view, so a helper can shadow a model or controller method and the collision appears only at render time.
html_safe (and raw) disables escaping for the whole string: interpolating user data into an html_safe string is the standard Rails XSS bug.
Helpers are instance methods of the view context, so the controller's instance variables are reachable and tempting to use - that coupling makes them hard to reuse and to test.
Locale-sensitive helpers (number_to_currency, distance_of_time_in_words) depend on I18n configuration; without locale defaults they fall back to English output that ships unnoticed.
